recognize_zh: 高倍下脂肪細胞之間是一片大型細胞，細胞質豐富偏嗜雙色、核偏位、染色質呈泡狀並可見核仁，旁邊有小而深染的紅血球前驅細胞與左側一顆巨核細胞作對照，符合退行性（anaplastic）漿細胞。
features: Large atypical cells with abundant amphophilic to eosinophilic cytoplasm
Round to oval, often eccentric nuclei with vesicular chromatin and visible nucleoli
Some binucleated forms and moderate nuclear pleomorphism
Cells form a cohesive-appearing sheet between adipocytes
Few small dark erythroid precursors and a megakaryocyte at the left edge for size comparison
describe_en: High-power view of the bone marrow biopsy shows a sheet of large atypical cells between adipocytes. The cells have abundant amphophilic cytoplasm, eccentric round to oval nuclei with vesicular chromatin and distinct nucleoli, with occasional binucleation. Rare residual erythroid precursors and a megakaryocyte at the left margin are present. Classic clock-face chromatin and perinuclear hofs are not prominent, so immunohistochemistry (CD138, kappa/lambda) is needed to confirm lineage. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma with anaplastic/plasmablastic cytology.

ddx.vs: Carcinoma cells form true glandular or cohesive nests and are cytokeratin-positive, whereas these cells are CD138/MUM1-positive and cytokeratin-negative plasma cells.
DLBCL cells express CD20/PAX5 and lack the abundant eccentric cytoplasm and CD138/light-chain restricted cytoplasmic immunoglobulin of plasma cells.
Plasmablastic lymphoma shares the CD138+/CD20- phenotype but typically occurs extramedullary in immunocompromised patients, is often EBER-positive, and lacks M-protein/lytic bone disease.
Megakaryocytes are much larger with lobulated nuclei and granular cytoplasm, as seen in the single megakaryocyte at the left edge, unlike the uniform round eccentric nuclei of plasma cells.
